title:
Comment of Jacci McKenna in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/31/2026

documents.name: 152013.txt
documents.text:
Jacci McKenna, Boulder, CO.
Beluga whales are echolocators, they use a biological sonar system to “see” in Cook Inlet’s dark, icy waters. They rely on sound to communicate, navigate, find food, and detect danger, making underwater noise a serious concern for their survival and recovery.

DeepGreen’s proposed project could likely contribute to hearing impairment, separation of family groups, loss of prey or habitat, disruption of biologically important feeding and mating areas, physical injury, and behavioral changes. The Beluga's already face a challenging environment, this proposal would make it even harder for them to survive.

In a five-year review, NOAA actually reported that several anthropogenic noise sources were found at levels with the potential to chronically mask beluga communication and hearing, and that shipping and dredging sounds exceeded behavioral-harassment levels daily in some monitored settings. And that was found before a 100-megawatt data center right in the middle of their critical habitat was proposed.

There are only an estimated 331 Belugas remaining in the Cook Inlet, the loss of even one Cook Inlet beluga whale is devastating to the current population, as well as to the recovery of this magnificent species.

FERC needs to evaluate what this project adds to the belugas existing burden; not pretend it’s being developed in a vacuum.
